problem: VLMs used for social robot navigation have poor spatial grounding (ambiguous relative positions, camera-relative directions) and there is little domain-specific annotated data for pedestrian interaction, so they produce faulty spatial reasoning and generic or ineffective actions.
motivation: Social navigation requires interpreting nuanced human motion and position relative to the robot, but manual annotation is expensive and existing datasets focus on driving. The authors observe that VLMs often reach wrong actions even when the high-level reasoning sounds plausible, because basic spatial perception is wrong.
key_idea: Fine-tune a small VLM on rule-based auto-labeled VQA pairs, built with a standardized spatial vocabulary, plus a few manual annotations, organized as a hierarchical two-round VQA (individual pedestrians first, then group and scene level).
insight: Auto-labeled data alone (AS-A0D1) barely improves over vanilla LLaVA, and manual data alone (LLaVA-M, 72 samples) is insufficient; only the combination gives the best scores (CODA 0.710 vs 0.404 and 0.376). The ablations show P&P-only VQA helps only P&P, while reasoning-only VQA helps R/A/E but not spatial perception, so the different VQA types complement each other. Halving manual annotations (A36) or downsampling the auto-labeled data has only a small effect, so a small amount of human supervision suffices.
method: Structured Spatial Grounding: pedestrian position is split into 5 angular zones (on the left ... on the right, by center pixel) and 5 distance levels (<3 m to >12 m); movement uses 8 compass directions plus stationary, with the robot's forward as north.

Auto-labeled VQA: rule-based heuristics on CODA trajectories and bounding boxes generate perception, movement prediction (start, continue, left/right turn, stop via sliding window and smoothed velocity) and interaction descriptions (conflict, crossing, pass-by, other), with no VLM involved.
Manual annotations: 72 hard CODA scenes (dense crowds, groups) annotated in the SNEI 5-task format (perception, prediction, CoT, action, explanation) following the spatial grounding guideline.

Two-round VQA: round 1 is auto-labeled individual-level QA; round 2, only for manually annotated scenes, refines to group dynamics and scene-level reasoning. Scenes with only auto labels use a single round.

Training: fine-tune LLaVA-1.6 OneVision-7B with default LLaVA instruction tuning (AdamW, lr 2e-5, batch 8, grad accumulation 4, 4xA100), with the grounding guideline in the system prompt and bounding boxes given only during training.

setting.training_data: CODA-derived rule-based auto-labeled VQA (6,205 training frames, 16,530 pedestrian instances; 18,615 pairs in total with the manual data) plus 72 manually annotated scenes in the SNEI format
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB image from a robot's perspective
setting.action_space: high-level textual social navigation action with explanation (no low-level control)
setting.simulator: none (offline evaluation on CODA images and SNEI)
setting.privileged: none at test time (bounding boxes and color-pedestrian correspondence are used only in training)

numbers.extra: 72 manual annotations plus all auto-labeled CODA VQA; scores are 1-10 from an LLM judge (Gemini 2.0 Flash here); the paper does not state which SNEI split was used
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Cross-Validation Scores, Gemini 2.0 flash columns, row AS-A72D1

numbers.eval_set_note: 573 test frames, 1,542 pedestrian instances (10% held-out auto-labeled CODA split)
numbers.extra: keyword-based score for direction and position (1.0 exact, 0.5 approximate)
numbers.evidence: Table 1, CODA Benchmark column: 0.710 vs LLaVA-M 0.404 and Vanilla-LLaVA 0.376

numbers.eval_set_note: 49 randomly sampled scenarios, 7 human evaluators, average rank (lower is better) among 3 models
numbers.extra: human relative ranking, not a score

numbers_note: The paper does not name the SNEI split. Claude 3.5 Sonnet judge scores are in Table 1 but are not repeated here; they are P&P 6.652, R 5.831, A 6.385, E 6.065 for AS-A72D1. The Table 1 Claude column header is misaligned with the data (one column appears missing). The paper does not evaluate on standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmarks.
results: AS-A72D1 scores 0.710 on the CODA spatial benchmark, against 0.404 for LLaVA-M and 0.376 for vanilla LLaVA. It also leads on most expert-judge scores (GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude) and in human rankings. The abstract reports gains over manual-only training of up to 10.71% (P&P), 16.26% (R), 20.50% (A) and 18.73% (E).
limitations: Evaluation is offline and judged by LLMs and 7 human raters on a 49-scene subset; there is no closed-loop or real-robot navigation test.
The model sometimes misreads gaze and body orientation and falls back to camera-relative descriptions instead of the structured grounding.
The spatial vocabulary and auto-labels are rule-based on CODA with discretized zones, and only 7B baselines are compared, not larger VLMs.
